body: [{"streamId":"01a1882f-489d-7225-9126-c342b8ac105f","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1882f-489d-7225-9126-c342b8ac105f\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022A solution groups one-repo projects: h9k solution add, show, list, link, unlink, rename and close, with the solution carried as a membership team setting on every member project, exactly one solution per project, and a cross-project board.\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022h9k solution add \\u003Cname\\u003E --project \\u003Cp\\u003E (repeatable) mints a solution key (a 26-character ULID) and writes a SolutionMembership into each named project\\u0027s team settings in that one command: the solution\\u0027s key and name, its state (open or closed) with a close reason, and every member by project key with its project name and repository URL. The name follows the rules a project name follows (unique on this node, case-insensitive), and every solution command resolves \\u003Cname\\u003E by name or key prefix. There is no separate Solution stream: the membership on the members is the solution.\u0022,\u0022The membership is one more optional team field, set through ProjectDecider.ChangeSettings and carried by ProjectTeamSettingsChanged.From, and every solution command appends the team companion the way h9k project set does, so it replicates with no new replication path, no new stream, and no change to EventReplicationInbox; the existing callers of ChangeSettings compile unchanged. A node that receives a membership for any member knows the whole solution from it, with nothing further to record.\u0022,\u0022A project belongs to at most one open solution, enforced in ProjectDecider.ChangeSettings: writing a membership with a different key onto a project whose current membership is open is refused, naming the solution it is in and pointing at h9k solution unlink. A closed membership does not hold the project. The setting is a single value in storage.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution add and link refuse a project with no recorded project key (naming h9k project join, or h9k project assign-key for the genesis owner) and a project with no recorded repository URL. Link, unlink, rename and close rewrite the membership on every member in one command, and refuse, naming the members, when any member is not registered and joined on this node.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution add and link warn and ask for confirmation when the new member\\u0027s repository owner or organization differs from every existing member\\u0027s; --yes answers it, and a session that cannot prompt refuses without --yes.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution rename and h9k solution close --reason are explicit human acts; close marks the membership closed with its reason on every member. Nothing closes a solution automatically, including every member being archived.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution show \\u003Cname\\u003E composes the solution\\u0027s board across members grouped by project, reusing TaskStatusComposer, TaskRollup and the project show task table, every row a task id plus a plain description; it lists members this node has not joined by name and repository URL, and shows a closed solution\\u0027s reason.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution list exists, h9k project show gains a Solution row, and task list and epic list accept --solution, resolved to the member projects known on this node.\u0022,\u0022Every new command and option carries help that teaches the ladder solution, project, epic, task, and every refusal quotes the rule it enforces. The commands that write are refused to dispatched sessions and show and list are read-only there, in DispatchedSessionCommandClassification.\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover the membership\\u0027s validation, the one-solution refusal, the team companion carrying the membership, a replicated membership landing on a second store\\u0027s project through the existing in-memory replication tests, the missing-key and not-held-here refusals, the owner-mismatch decision, and board composition; no test creates a branch or touches GitHub.\u0022,\u0022docs/scope.md, docs/concepts.md, docs/cli.md and the hall9k-cli-reference skill describe the solution concept and its commands.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Discovery for idea f8212260 is in the idea\\u0027s workspace: findings.md (the design, the name, the hard-to-reverse choices) and journal.md (Brian\\u0027s rulings on 2026-10-29); the challenge\\u0027s evidence is notes/challenge-b8ac105f/journal.md in the project home. Model the membership on ContextLinks: a named record, replace-the-whole-record semantics on ProjectTeamSettingsChanged, a repeatable flag. Members are named by project key (the 26-character ULID from the ledger genesis, identical across nodes), never by local project id. The challenge of 2026-10-29, accepted by Brian, dropped the node-scoped SolutionAggregate the findings first described: nothing on main mints a local stream from a received event, and a node-scoped close would never reach the other nodes, so the membership itself carries the name, state and close reason. The one-solution rule exists for a security reason Brian gave: a project in two solutions would put each solution\\u0027s member names and repository URLs in front of the other solution\\u0027s teammates. Two nodes linking one project into different solutions at the same moment resolve as last write wins on replication; that is parked until it first happens. This piece changes nothing in dispatch, delivery, review, closeout or the gh layer. It is the base of a stack: solution epics stack on it, the solution window and onboarding are blocked by it, and the solution home in the window card is named after the solution\\u0027s name.\u0022},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-29T15:37:59.145416\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Effort\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"694e3402-858e-4539-8eb8-8ecc794e0c22","originSequence":140094,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-29T15:37:59.158191+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a1882f-8e3a-7000-ac09-37929e4998eb","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1882f-8e3a-7000-ac09-37929e4998eb\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022In a project that belongs to a solution every epic is a solution epic, created at once in every member project this node holds and open to tasks from any member, and a second task may hold a shared tracker issue when it sits in the same solution epic in a different member project.\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022h9k epic add --project \\u003Cp\\u003E, where p belongs to a solution, creates one solution epic: every member project this node holds gets its own copy, all copies share one solution epic key and the title, and each copy replicates through its own project\\u0027s ledger exactly as an epic does today. The command names any member this node does not hold, which receives no copy from it.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution link and h9k solution add give a newly linked project a copy of every open solution epic this node holds for that solution, so a project linked later can take tasks under the solution\\u0027s existing epics.\u0022,\u0022A project inside a solution cannot create a project-only epic; epics a project held before it was linked stay project epics, and a project outside any solution behaves exactly as today.\u0022,\u0022A task from any member project may join a solution epic at task add --epic or task revise --epic by naming the solution epic key or any copy\\u0027s id; the task joins its own project\\u0027s copy, and a task from a project outside the solution, or a closed epic, is still refused.\u0022,\u0022epic show and epic list show a solution epic as one epic: one row with the solution named, and member tasks across projects grouped by project. epic list --project \\u003Cmember\\u003E includes the solution\\u0027s epics, and a node shows only the tasks of projects it has joined.\u0022,\u0022The one-live-task-per-issue refusal (TaskAddCommand.RefuseSecondAdoptionAsync, reached from --from-issue, --from-jira, task link-issue and task link-jira) admits a new task only when that task is in a solution epic and every live holder of the issue is in the same solution epic in a different member project. The new task\\u0027s epic is read from --epic at add time and from the task itself at link time. Every other case refuses with today\\u0027s message, and a holder outside the epic is named with the remedy of joining it to the epic first.\u0022,\u0022When a task closes out and its issue is also held by a task in another member project, closeout closes the issue only if this node holds every member project of the solution and every other linked task is done or abandoned (CloseoutEngine.AllOtherLinkedTasksClosedOutAsync); otherwise the issue stays open and the closeout line says why.\u0022,\u0022Unlinking a project from its solution leaves that project\\u0027s copies and every task under them where they are, still shown on the solution epic; later solution epics and later closes no longer reach it, and the project may create project epics again.\u0022,\u0022Closing a solution epic stays an explicit human act with a reason; it closes every copy this node holds, and nothing closes one automatically.\u0022,\u0022Tests cover copy creation across held members, link-time copies, the same-solution join, the one-row composition, the shared-issue admission and its refusals, the closeout guard, and unlink. Store-backed cases join an existing shared store-backed class rather than adding a container, and no test creates a branch or touches GitHub.\u0022,\u0022docs/concepts.md, docs/scope.md and the hall9k-cli-reference skill describe solution epics, the shared-issue rule, the closeout guard and unlink behaviour.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Discovery for idea f8212260: findings.md and journal.md in the idea\\u0027s workspace; the challenge\\u0027s evidence is notes/challenge-9e4998eb/journal.md in the project home. Brian\\u0027s rulings (2026-10-29): no home project; in a solution project every epic is solution-wide, so every member knows of it before any task exists; a second task may hold one tracker issue only inside the same solution epic and a different member project (the case of one issue needing a backend and a frontend change, raised by the Linear connector discovery, idea 5d12221a). Mechanism, chosen at challenge and accepted by Brian: a solution epic is one ordinary epic per member project, all carrying a shared solution epic key (one trailing optional field on EpicAdded, so existing streams replay unchanged). No replication code changes: ReplicationProjectResolver, EventReplicationOutbox, EventReplicationInbox and EventCatchUpResponder each resolve a stream to exactly one project, and teaching them otherwise would reopen the inbox\\u0027s stream-ownership guard. An older build sees each copy as a plain project epic, which is the right fallback. Closeout\\u0027s linked-task check reads only tasks this node holds, which is why the closeout criterion guards on holding every member. Stacked on the solution base task because it reads the SolutionMembership type and the solution key that task introduces, and it changes the epic list --solution option that task adds.\u0022},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-29T15:38:15.258445\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Effort\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"4ffdd0aa-0148-4152-96ce-a6bd2bf31a26","originSequence":140095,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-29T15:38:15.268808+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"}]
